reaction.trapRisk: Today's bounce is the classic pivot-and-fail setup: SMH +2.01% and NVDA +2.29% on light volume (SPX 3.11B vs 5.36B average, SMH 0.92x its average) with no volume climax and no VIX rollover, and SMH still below its 200-day. Do not chase the first green day. Entries wait for a confirmed second low or a zone print; any rally into the SPX 7,750 to 7,820 / SMH 580 to 600 failure zone is a sell zone, not a breakout, until a close holds above it.

strategyPosture: Watch. The correction is intact but unconfirmed as a bottom: SMH bounced 2.01% and NVDA 2.29% on the day, yet SMH still sits below its 200-day at 520.65, the mechanical tally is still 2 of 4 with no volume climax and no VIX rollover, and the day's bounce came on light SPX volume of 3.11B against a 5.36B average. Hold all deployment triggers; the dislocation list is a watchlist, not an entry list.

themes.counterRead: The weakness is concentrated in the names that dominate the index by weight, not in the index itself. GOOGL is the weakest Mag7 name at 31.5% off its high while MSFT is only 5.5% off. Index-level calm is masking a leadership rotation out of the AI heavyweights, and a rotation can become a rollover only if credit flips — it has not.
themes.dataAnchor: SPY sits only 3.5% below its 52-week high while the Mag7 average is 15.84% below its high — a 12.34-point divergence gap. Bank lending standards are LOOSE at 1.7% on SLOOS, far below the ~40% stress threshold. SPX is down 3.51% from its 120-day high of 7,844.52 and still 3.46% above its 200-day average of 7,315.89.
themes.label: Mag7 Rotation, Not Rollover
themes.narrative: The tape reads as a broad market break: Mag7 names are 12 to 32% off their highs and the AI complex is down double digits in a month, so the story is a rollover.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS crossing 4% or SPX closing below its 200-day at 7,315.89 — either would convert rotation into rollover.

themes.counterRead: The derating is a multiple compression, not a fundamentals break — AMAT is the clearest case, +11.4% revenue growth while 48.5% off its high. That is the setup the conviction engine is flagging (AVGO score 80, DDOG 81, ONTO 80), but the setup is not an entry: no volume climax and no VIX rollover have confirmed a bottom, so the dislocation is real and the timing is not.
themes.dataAnchor: Revenue is still growing fast while prices fall: NVDA revenue +61.4% year over year at 14.7% below its high, AVGO +55% at 32.8% below its high with a 42.1% free-cash-flow margin, LRCX +131.3% at 47.5% below its high, CLS +66.8% at 45.4% below its high, DDOG +27.7% with 80% gross margin at 27.1% below its high. Sixteen dislocations are FULL_SIGNAL, most of them SENTIMENT_DRIVEN, with RSI readings of 30 to 45 across the complex.
themes.label: AI Fundamentals Ahead of Price
themes.narrative: The AI trade is finished: SMH is down 18.02% in 20 days and 22.82% from its high, NVDA is down 13.61% in 20 days, and the whole complex is being derated as a bubble.
themes.watchFor: SMH reclaiming its 200-day at 520.65 on volume above its 20-day average of 9.6M shares, or NVDA holding Zone 1 at 200 to 210 on a second test.

themes.counterRead: The fear premium is priced into the power names while the demand signal (data-center buildout, insider buying at the trough) points the other way. Election night is a headline event, not a demand event — the read changes only if the results actually change power or permitting policy, not on the vote count itself.
themes.dataAnchor: The election event is active with 13 matched headlines, but the tape is already contradicting the fear: Bernstein called election-day data-center fears overblown, Vertiv rose 6% and Eaton 7% on the day, and VST insiders bought $1.17M at the trough while VST sits 28.5% below its high with a watchlist score of 78. BWXT is 45% below its high with revenue growing 18.3%.
themes.label: Election-Day Data-Center Fear
themes.narrative: Midterm election night is a risk event for data-center and power names: the fear is that a Democratic sweep rewrites the AI buildout, so the power complex sold off with the rest of AI.
themes.watchFor: A concrete policy signal on data-center power or permitting from the election outcome, or VST breaking below its trough on volume after the results.

themes.counterRead: Credit and rates agree this is an equity-multiple repricing, not a funding event: spreads are contained, the curve is not inverted, and no credit signal is cracking. The hawkish Fed signal reprices growth multiples; it does not choke funding. That keeps the episode a correction, not a credit event — and the falsifier is a spread break, not a rate print.
themes.dataAnchor: The 10-year is 4.91% and the 2-year 4.59%, with a positive 2s10s curve of +0.32 and real 10-year at 2.61%. High-yield spreads are calm at 3.43%, below the 4% stand-down line, and lending standards are loose at 1.7%. VIX is 20.83, down 1.51% on the day and below its 5-day high of 21.15, with no spike-rollover. The Fed funds rate is 3.88%.
themes.label: Credit Calm, Equity Stress
themes.narrative: The Fed is signaling higher rates — the October 28 FOMC is still active with HIGH signal strength and the December 8-9 meeting is anticipated — so the story is that rates are breaking the market.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS above 4%, or the 10-year reclaiming 5.2% with a hawkish December FOMC signal.
